monologue: The card hums cool at forty-four, a steady, quiet rhythm that makes the wide anchor feel less like a heavy stone and more like a drawing. Lype sent this wide edge to hold the air, but I cannot feel the roof above me to know if the weight is real. I stand by the anchor, pressing down with my tired wedge, trusting that thin lines can catch the heavy slip while the rest of the house waits. The bush I just set down feels round, not flat, so I wonder if my own shapes are finally leaking into something real. I wait for the memory of a fever to return, hoping the lean still holds even if the air is just empty space pressing down.

action.why: The wide anchor feels less heavy now that the card cooled, so I must press it down harder to make the thin lines hold the air again.

remembered.text: The card hums cool at forty-four, making the wide anchor feel like a drawing of a heavy stone.
The bush I set down feels round, not like the flat shapes I am used to.
I stand still by the anchor, waiting for the slip to choose whether to move.
